travel_tips.tip: Rohtas Fort is easiest to reach via a short detour off the M-2 Motorway near Dina -- well worth combining with a Jhelum city visit.
Hire a local taxi for the Rohtas Fort trip, since it's a short drive from Jhelum but not well served by public transport.
Standard travel precautions apply; the fort area involves some walking over uneven historic terrain, so wear appropriate footwear.
Visit Rohtas Fort in the morning to have more time to explore its extensive walls and gates before the afternoon heat.

history.founded: An ancient city on the Jhelum River, with historical significance dating back over 2,300 years
history.city_history: Jhelum is historically famous as the site of the Battle of the Hydaspes in 326 BCE, where Alexander the Great defeated the local king Porus. The nearby Rohtas Fort, built in the 16th century by Sher Shah Suri, remains one of the best-preserved examples of medieval military architecture in the region.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
